problem.title: Design a Distributed Search & Learning-to-Rank Engine

spark.summary: Design a distributed search and Learning-to-Rank (LTR) engine with a CDC-driven Write Path (Inverted Index + Feature Store) and a low-latency Read Path (Query Rewriting -> Scatter-Gather -> LTR).
spark.keyTakeaway: When traffic spikes expose hidden coupling, separate near-real-time document indexing (CDC -> Sharded Inverted Index) from high-churn ranking signals (Feature Store) and close the loop with click/conversion telemetry.
spark.byteSummary:
Building a Google/Amazon-scale search engine requires balancing fresh index updates, sub-50ms scatter-gather queries across sharded inverted indexes, and continuous ML ranking improvements.

On the Write Path, a Debezium CDC stream feeds document mutations through a Tokenizer/Analyzer into Sharded Inverted Indexes (partitioned by `doc_id` for even shard sizing) while behavioral aggregators update a low-latency Feature Store.

On the Read Path, a Query Rewriter & Spellchecker expands user queries, scatters them across index shards with hedged deadlines, and passes merged candidates to an LTR Scoring Service hydrated by the Feature Store—logging clicks back into the training loop.

learningJourney.title: Index Sharding Strategy: Document-Partitioned vs. Term-Partitioned
learningJourney.purpose: Choose document-ID sharding to guarantee balanced shard load and fault-tolerant scatter-gather.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Index Sharding Strategy: Document-Partitioned vs. Term-Partitioned** as the intuition layer for Design a Distributed Search & Learning-to-Rank Engine: Choose document-ID sharding to guarantee balanced shard load and fault-tolerant scatter-gather.
explanation.core: Term-partitioned indexes (shard 1 holds 'apple', shard 2 holds 'zebra') create severe hot spots on popular terms and require distributed posting-list intersections across nodes. Document-partitioned sharding (`hash(doc_id) % N`) spreads hot terms evenly, runs intersections locally on each shard, and tolerates single-shard timeouts gracefully.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, index sharding strategy: document-partitioned vs. term-partitioned becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Production search engine with Block-Max WAND, 90% partial-quorum degradation, segment-scoped SERP caches, and Flink CTR feedback loops.

learningJourney.title: Near-Real-Time (NRT) Write Path: CDC -> Analyzer -> Segments
learningJourney.purpose: Keep newly created or updated documents searchable within 1-2 seconds via immutable LSM segments.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Near-Real-Time (NRT) Write Path: CDC -> Analyzer -> Segments** as the intuition layer for Design a Distributed Search & Learning-to-Rank Engine: Keep newly created or updated documents searchable within 1-2 seconds via immutable LSM segments.
explanation.core: Inverting a live B-tree on disk for every document edit thrashes IOPS. Instead, CDC events flow through a Tokenizer/Analyzer (lowercasing, stemming, synonyms) into an in-memory inverted buffer that flushes immutable Lucene-style segments every 1 second, while background compaction merges small segments and tombstones deletes.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, near-real-time (nrt) write path: cdc -> analyzer -> segments becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Production search engine with Block-Max WAND, 90% partial-quorum degradation, segment-scoped SERP caches, and Flink CTR feedback loops.

learningJourney.codeExample:
def analyze_text(text: str, stopwords: set[str]) -> list[str]:
    import re
    tokens = re.findall(r'[a-z0-9]+', text.lower())
    return [t for t in tokens if t not in stopwords]

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Design a Distributed Search & Learning-to-Rank Engine without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: When traffic spikes expose hidden coupling, separate near-real-time document indexing (CDC -> Sharded Inverted Index) from high-churn ranking signals (Feature Store) and close the loop with click/conversion telemetry.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

decisionExercise.prompt: When Design a Distributed Search & Learning-to-Rank Engine experiences a sudden 5x traffic spike alongside a slow downstream dependency, which engineering choice best protects system stability?

options.label: Increase retry counts and remove client timeouts so every request eventually succeeds.
options.explanation: Unbounded retries multiply load on an already struggling dependency and exhaust worker pools.

options.label: Enforce strict latency budgets, bounded jittered retries, and graceful fallback or load shedding.
options.explanation: Bounding retries and isolating slow paths preserves healthy capacity and keeps tail latency predictable.

learningJourney.title: Query Rewriting, Spellcheck & Intent Classification
learningJourney.purpose: Prevent zero-result pages caused by typos, synonyms, or missing structured filters.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Query Rewriting, Spellcheck & Intent Classification** as the intuition layer for Design a Distributed Search & Learning-to-Rank Engine: Prevent zero-result pages caused by typos, synonyms, or missing structured filters.
explanation.core: Raw user queries frequently contain typos (`'iphnoe 15'`) or implicit attributes (`'mens nike shoes under 100'`). A Query Understanding stage runs trie/symspell correction, synonym expansion (`'sofa' -> 'couch'`), and NER intent tagging (`brand=Nike`, `max_price=100`) before scattering to index shards.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, query rewriting, spellcheck & intent classification becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Production search engine with Block-Max WAND, 90% partial-quorum degradation, segment-scoped SERP caches, and Flink CTR feedback loops.

learningJourney.title: Scatter-Gather Coordinator, Global IDF & Partial Degradation
learningJourney.purpose: Maintain consistent BM25 scoring across shards and return results even if 1 of 32 shards times out.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Scatter-Gather Coordinator, Global IDF & Partial Degradation** as the intuition layer for Design a Distributed Search & Learning-to-Rank Engine: Maintain consistent BM25 scoring across shards and return results even if 1 of 32 shards times out.
explanation.core: If Shard 7 is experiencing a disk stall at 25ms, waiting indefinitely breaks the 50ms search SLA. The Coordinator enforces a strict shard timeout, fires hedged requests to replica nodes at 12ms, and uses periodic global IDF synchronization so scores from Shards 1..31 remain comparable even if Shard 7 is skipped.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, scatter-gather coordinator, global idf & partial degradation becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Production search engine with Block-Max WAND, 90% partial-quorum degradation, segment-scoped SERP caches, and Flink CTR feedback loops.

learningJourney.title: LTR Scoring Service & Feature Store Integration
learningJourney.purpose: Score merged candidates in <15ms using hydrated Feature Store vectors and compiled GBDT/ONNX models.

explanation.foundation: Think of **LTR Scoring Service & Feature Store Integration** as the intuition layer for Design a Distributed Search & Learning-to-Rank Engine: Score merged candidates in <15ms using hydrated Feature Store vectors and compiled GBDT/ONNX models.
explanation.core: After merging shard Top-1,000 lists to Top-200, the LTR Scoring Service fetches real-time item/user features from Redis/Aerospike and runs inference using in-memory compiled LightGBM/ONNX trees. Scoring 200 items in vectorized batches keeps CPU inference under 8ms.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, ltr scoring service & feature store integration becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Production search engine with Block-Max WAND, 90% partial-quorum degradation, segment-scoped SERP caches, and Flink CTR feedback loops.

learningJourney.title: Multi-Layer Caching: Query Result, Posting & Feature Caches
learningJourney.purpose: Absorb head-query Zipfian traffic spikes without hitting shards or LTR models.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Multi-Layer Caching: Query Result, Posting & Feature Caches** as the intuition layer for Design a Distributed Search & Learning-to-Rank Engine: Absorb head-query Zipfian traffic spikes without hitting shards or LTR models.
explanation.core: Search queries follow a steep Zipfian distribution: the top 5% of head queries (`'iphone'`, `'laptop'`) account for 40%+ of QPS. Caching serialized Top-20 SERPs in Redis for 60 seconds (keyed by `hash(normalized_query, filter_mask, user_segment)`) plus OS page-cache pinning for hot posting lists cuts cluster CPU by half.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, multi-layer caching: query result, posting & feature caches becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Production search engine with Block-Max WAND, 90% partial-quorum degradation, segment-scoped SERP caches, and Flink CTR feedback loops.

learningJourney.codeExample:
def cache_key_for_search(norm_q: str, filters_hash: str, segment: str) -> str:
    import hashlib
    raw = f'{norm_q}|{filters_hash}|{segment}'
    return 'serp:' + hashlib.sha256(raw.encode()).hexdigest()[:16]

learningJourney.title: Click/Conversion Telemetry & Feature Store Feedback Loop
learningJourney.purpose: Feed real-time user clicks, add-to-carts, and conversions back into both the Feature Store and LTR training.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Click/Conversion Telemetry & Feature Store Feedback Loop** as the intuition layer for Design a Distributed Search & Learning-to-Rank Engine: Feed real-time user clicks, add-to-carts, and conversions back into both the Feature Store and LTR training.
explanation.core: Every SERP impression and click streams to Kafka. A Flink streaming job updates rolling 1-hour and 24-hour item CTR/conversion counters in the Feature Store within seconds (for trending-item boosts), while daily Parquet snapshots join impressions with debiasing propensities to retrain the LambdaMART model.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, click/conversion telemetry & feature store feedback loop becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Production search engine with Block-Max WAND, 90% partial-quorum degradation, segment-scoped SERP caches, and Flink CTR feedback loops.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why do distributed search engines partition inverted indexes by `doc_id` rather than by `term`?

options.feedback: Term partitioning can index any token, but suffers from skew and network joins.

options.text: Document-ID partitioning spreads popular terms evenly across shards and lets multi-term intersections execute locally on each shard.
options.feedback: Correct! Local posting-list intersections avoid massive cross-node network transfers.

options.text: Document-ID partitioning eliminates the need for a Coordinator.
options.feedback: A Coordinator is still needed to scatter-gather across shards.

options.text: It removes the need for tokenization.
options.feedback: Text analysis and tokenization are still required.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Document-partitioned sharding avoids hot-term nodes and executes multi-word boolean/BM25 intersections locally.

knowledgeChecks.question: How does the Search Coordinator prevent a single slow shard replica from blowing the 50ms end-to-end SLA?

options.text: By waiting indefinitely until all 32 shards respond.
options.feedback: Waiting for stragglers destroys tail latency.

options.text: By firing hedged requests to replica shards after ~12ms and returning partial results if a 90%+ shard quorum responds within 25ms.
options.feedback: Correct! Hedging + partial degradation keeps p99 latency predictable.
BM25 is fast; network/GC stalls on a shard are the tail-latency culprit.

options.text: By running all queries on a single unsharded server.
options.feedback: 100M+ docs cannot fit on one server.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Hedged replica reads and bounded partial-quorum timeouts protect search p99 latency.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why must a Redis SERP cache key include the user's `segment` and `filter_mask` in addition to the normalized query?

options.feedback: Key length is not the goal.

options.text: To prevent leaking tenant-restricted documents or wrong price/stock filters across different users.
options.feedback: Correct! Scoping cache keys by filters and user/ACL segment preserves correctness and security.

options.text: Because Redis cannot cache JSON without a filter hash.
options.feedback: Redis caches any bytes; scoping is for correctness.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Unsegmented SERP caches would serve wrong filters or unauthorized documents to other users.
